papers.title_in_file: Quantum Picturalism: Learning Quantum Theory in High School
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, methodology (sample, design, assessment), discussion and conclusion; the course-content appendix and reference list were skimmed only.
papers.what_it_is: A 2023 methodology paper from Quantinuum and Oxford that sets out a diagram-based (Quantum Picturalism) way to teach quantum theory to high-school students and describes an ongoing teaching experiment.

assertions.value: The authors state that the paper establishes the foundations and methodology for an ongoing educational experiment asking from what age students can learn quantum theory when taught with a diagrammatic approach.
quotes: We establish the foundations and methodology for an ongoing educational experiment to investigate the question
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own scope.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper reports a design, not outcomes; it cannot be cited as evidence that the approach works.

assertions.value: The authors report a post-test intervention trial that recruited 75 volunteer high-school students aged 16 to 19 by purposive sampling.
quotes: A purposive sampling approach was employed to recruit 75 volunteer high-school students aged 16 to 19.
evidence has been collected using a post-test design to evaluate the effectiveness of the QP approach
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup.
assertions.reader_inference: A post-test-only design with volunteers and no control group limits what the later results can show.

assertions.value: The authors state that more evidence is needed to test the approach against diverse control groups and to explore its effects on larger samples of the high-school student population.
quotes: More evidence will be needed to test against diverse control groups, and to explore the effects of QP on larger samples of the high-school student population.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own limits.

papers.title_in_file: Permutation Invariant Encodings for Quantum Machine Learning with Point Cloud Data
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results, discussion and conclusion; encoding derivation skimmed; appendices not read.
papers.what_it_is: A numerical study of a permutation-invariant quantum encoding for point cloud data, used inside a quantum support vector machine.

assertions.value: The authors report that a permutation invariant encoding improves in accuracy as the number of points in the point cloud increases, while non-invariant quantum encodings decrease in accuracy.
quotes: We show that a permutation invariant encoding improves in accuracy as the number of points contained in the point cloud increases, while non-invariant quantum encodings decrease in accuracy.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one simulation study on one synthetic task.

assertions.value: The authors state that the tests are numerical simulations of a Quantum Support Vector Machine classifying point clouds drawn from spherical or toroidal geometries, and that the results were obtained from noiseless simulations.
quotes: We test this encoding method in numerical simulations using a Quantum Support Vector Machine to classify point clouds drawn from either spherical or toroidal geometries.
Our results were obtained from noiseless simulations using Qiskit
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup and scope.
assertions.reader_inference: No hardware or noisy result is reported, so the finding is a simulator result on a synthetic two-class task.

assertions.value: The authors report that for small datasets the permutation invariant quantum encoding outperforms both non-invariant quantum and classical methods and the classical method PointNet, and that for larger data samples PointNet starts to approach its accuracy.
quotes: quantum encoding outperforms both non-invariant quantum/classical methods and the permutation-invariant classical method PointNet.
For larger data samples, PointNet starts to approach the accuracy of the permutation invariant QSVM encoding.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study; the advantage is stated for small datasets only.

assertions.value: The authors state that the work demonstrates an encoding method that improves generalisation for permutation invariant data but does not necessarily guarantee that a quantum advantage exists, and that efficient implementation on real devices and behaviour under noise remain open.
quotes: This work demonstrates an encoding method to improve generalisation for permutation invariant data, however, it does not necessarily guarantee a quantum advantage exists.
is also the possible challenge of finding an efficient implementation on real devices and assessing how the encodings will perform in the presence of noise.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own limits.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Optimization Methods for Satellite Mission Planning
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, methods overview, results discussion and conclusions; formulation details skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: An experimental study of quantum annealing and QAOA on satellite mission planning instances, with constraint encodings.

assertions.value: The authors state that they use 31 problem instances to evaluate quantum annealing and QAOA on available hardware and simulators, of which six come from the SPOT5 dataset and the remaining 25 were generated from SPOT5.
quotes: We use 31 different problem instances to evaluate our formulation as well as the performance of quantum annealing and QAOA methods on currently available quantum hardware and simulators.
while the remaining 25 were generated based on SPOT5 using an instance reductor specifically implemented for this study.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup.

assertions.value: The authors report that quantum annealing handled instances of up to about 80 requests when no capacity constraints were included, and that QAOA reached more modest instance sizes, limited by the number of qubits they could simulate.
quotes: With QA, we were able to tackle instances with sizes of up to about 80 requests
although we were limited by the number of qubits we were able to simulate.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study on one dataset family.
assertions.reader_inference: The 80-request figure is for the no-capacity case only; the capacity-constrained size is not captured in the quotes.

assertions.value: The authors state that even in ideal simulated environments the performance of QAOA is generally not on par with quantum annealing, and that solution quality degrades with problem size, imposing practical limits on the instances that can currently be solved effectively.
assertions.anchor: Conclusions and further work, pages 11 to 12
quotes: With respect to the QAOA, even in ideal simulated environments, the performance is generally not on par with QA.
shown how the quality of the solutions degrades with problem size, imposing practical limits on the instances that can currently be solved effectively
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study.

papers.title_in_file: State estimation with quantum extreme learning machines beyond the scrambling time
papers.version_note: File is arXiv v2 of 7 Feb 2025.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, main results and conclusions; methods section skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A numerical study relating quantum information scrambling to the state-estimation accuracy of quantum extreme learning machines.

assertions.value: The authors report that efficient state estimation with a quantum extreme learning machine is possible even beyond the scrambling time for many different types of dynamics.
quotes: we show efficient state estimation is possible even beyond the scrambling time, for many different types of dynamics
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from numerical studies of a limited set of reservoirs.

assertions.value: The authors report that in all the cases they studied, the reconstruction efficiency at long interaction times matches the optimal one offered by random global unitary dynamics.
quotes: in all the cases we studied, the reconstruction efficiency at long interaction times matches the optimal one offered by random global unitary dynamics.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result limited to the cases studied.

assertions.value: The authors state that the reservoir size studied runs from 2 to 7 qubits, and they qualify their conclusion about scrambling systems as holding at least for relatively small systems.
quotes: from 2 to 7 qubits
at least for relatively small systems
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own scope and limits.
assertions.reader_inference: The result is not shown for large reservoirs.

papers.what_it_is: A proposal and simulation study of a slimmable quantum federated learning framework that adapts to time-varying communication channels.

assertions.value: The authors report that simulation results show SlimQFL achieves higher classification accuracy than Vanilla QFL, particularly under poor channel conditions on average.
quotes: Simulation results corroborate that SlimQFL achieves higher classification accuracy than Vanilla QFL, particularly under poor channel conditions on average.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical simulation result from one study on a reduced task.

assertions.value: The authors state that performance is measured as top-1 accuracy on a mini-MNIST task with 4 labels, all experiments use independent and identically distributed data, and the reduced task is chosen because quantum computing suffers from a lack of input qubits.
quotes: The performance is measured using the top-1 accuracy in an MNIST classification task.
Compared to MNIST, mini-MNIST consists of 4 labels
Since quantum computing suffers from the lack of input qubits, we consider a mini-version of the MNIST
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup and scope.
assertions.reader_inference: The result rests on a small simulated task, not a realistic federated workload.

assertions.value: The authors state that analyzing the convergence of SlimQFL under various channel conditions and under non-IID global data distributions is left as a future topic.
quotes: it could be an interesting topic to analyze the convergence of SlimQFL under various communication channel conditions as well as global data distributions that would be non-IID.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own limits.
assertions.reader_inference: No convergence guarantee and no non-IID result is given.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Vision Transformers for Quark-Gluon Classification
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, model description, results and conclusions; background sections skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A hybrid quantum-classical vision transformer with variational circuits in attention and MLP layers, tested in simulation on CMS Open Data quark versus gluon jet images.

assertions.value: The authors report that the hybrid QViT obtains almost the same ROC curve and AUC score as the classical baseline, though it lags by approximately two percentage points; the Figure 8 legend gives AUC 0.793 for the classical model and 0.775 for the quantum model.
quotes: We observe that the proposed QViT results in almost the same ROC curve and obtains almost the same AUC score as the classical baseline, though it still lags by approximately two percentage points.
Classical (AUC = 0.793) Quantum (AUC = 0.775)
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study; the quantum model did not exceed the baseline.
assertions.reader_inference: No quantum advantage is shown; the quantum model is slightly behind.

assertions.value: The authors state that the VQCs are executed by numerical simulation on a classical computer, and that the classical ViT has 5178 parameters while the QViT has 4170 parameters.
quotes: We use TensorCircuit [64] to implement, train, and execute the VQCs by numerical simulation on a classical computer.
In total, the classical ViT has 5178 parameters, while the QViT has 4170 parameters.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that the proposed VQCs might lack the expressiveness required to match or exceed the classical model, and that running the VQCs on real quantum hardware to assess robustness to quantum noise is future work.
quotes: Alternatively, the proposed VQCs might lack the expressiveness required to match or exceed the performance of the classical model.
Finally, we would also like to execute the VQCs on real quantum hardware to measure the performance of the proposed QViT in it
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own limits.

assertions.value: The authors report that, for certain testing cases, the quantum version of LSTM converges faster, or equivalently reaches a better accuracy, than its classical counterpart.
quotes: we show that for certain testing cases, this quantum version of LSTM converges faster, or equivalently, reaches a better accuracy, than its classical counterpart.

papers.title_in_file: Neural Quantum Embedding: Pushing the Limits of Quantum Supervised Learning
papers.version_note: File is arXiv v2 of 9 Aug 2024.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, experiments, generalization section and conclusions; proofs in the appendices skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A method that trains a classical neural network to optimize quantum embeddings, with theory, simulations and IBM hardware experiments on MNIST images.

assertions.value: The authors report experiments on IBM quantum devices for image data classification with an accuracy enhancement from 0.52 to 0.96, and state that accuracy reached 96% (PCA-NQE) and 90% (NQE) while the conventional method achieved only 52%.
quotes: we conduct experiments on IBM quantum devices for image data classification, resulting in a remarkable accuracy enhancement from 0.52 to 0.96
a substantial improvement in classification accuracy was recorded, reaching 96% (PCA-NQE) and 90% (NQE), whereas the conventional method achieved only 52%.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study on a two-class MNIST subset.
assertions.reader_inference: The baseline is the ZZ feature embedding on a four-qubit task; the gain does not show an advantage over strong classical models.

assertions.value: The authors state that the main experiments use a four-qubit Quantum Convolutional Neural Network to classify images of 0 and 1 from the MNIST dataset, in noiseless simulation and on IBM cloud quantum devices.
quotes: we employed a four-qubit Quantum Convolutional Neural Network (QCNN)
classifying images of 0 and 1 within the MNIST dataset
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup and scope.

assertions.value: The authors state that the training performance achieved by NQE is guaranteed to be at least as good as that of approaches relying on a fixed embedding function, because NQE would learn the fixed function if it happened to be optimal.
quotes: The training performance achieved by NQE is guaranteed to be at least as good as those that do not use it and rely on a fixed embedding function.
This is because if the fixed embedding function happens to be the optimal one for the given data, NQE will learn to use it.
assertions.certainty_reason: An argument stated in the conclusions, not a formal proof at this location.
assertions.reader_inference: The guarantee concerns the training objective, not test accuracy.

assertions.value: The authors state that further research is necessary on the impact of the neural network type or architecture on NQE performance and on its optimization for specific types of target data.
quotes: Further research is necessary to explore the impact of the type or architecture of neural networks on the performance of NQE, and its optimization for specific types of target data.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own limits.
